thesis_project.title: Automating Terrain Generation Using Wave Function Collapse
long: For the Computing and the Arts major, I explored procedural terrain generation — stemming from both a personal interest in video games and an intersection between both fields. While I enjoy the intricacy and level of detail of hand-crafted environments, the creation process is often time-consuming and difficult to scale. Purely algorithmic generation, while fast and endlessly customizable, frequently lacks a distinct visual identity and is difficult to modify for unique art styles and odd geometry.

To mitigate the drawbacks of both approaches while retaining scalability, configurability, and aesthetics, the Wave Function Collapse (WFC) was explored and implemented. WFC finds seamless connections between hand-made modular assets to build a series of adjacency rules: four rotations per asset and six connection points per rotation. The algorithm begins with an empty 3D grid whose cells exist in multiple states — one per asset rotation. The primary loop finds and collapses the cell with the fewest possibilities into a single state, propagating that information outward and eliminating states in neighboring cells that would violate adjacency rules. The loop terminates if a cell with zero possibilities is encountered or when all cells are collapsed.

Blender, its Python API, and Unity were utilized to model and program the project. For its installation in the Undergraduate Thesis Exhibition, I presented a visual representation of the algorithm building its terrain, accompanied by gradients to highlight its modular nature and sounds for every asset placement.
short: Created for the Computing and the Arts major, this project explored the Wave Function Collapse algorithm to generate customizable, visually distinctive terrain using Blender, Python, and Unity.

game_engine.title: Building a Game Engine: Defending Your Farm
long: I incrementally built a video game engine in a semester-long course taught in the DLang. Throughout a variety of exercises, including replicating Super Mario Bros. and Space Invaders, I implemented and refined game objects, their respective components (texture, transform, collision, animation), custom scripts, input managers, acceleration-based movement, trailing cameras, and scene trees.

Our final project was a group assignment of two parts: building a tile set editor and a video game of at least three levels. Our group “BAPI” (an acronym of our first names) developed a charming farming game with defensive and offensive mechanics, defending crops from hostile entities to harvest enough produce to advance to the following level.

My contributions to the project include most player functions (input, movement, and interactions with collision blocks, tools, weapons, and enemies); tilemap, world, and array conversions (storing game objects as array entries, placing them at world coordinates, and spawning them from tilemap data); and game entity interactions (player with tools, tools with the game world, weapons with enemies, enemies with planted crops, and enemies with the player).
short: Built a farming game using a custom game engine, contributing player controls, world-to-data conversion systems, and interactions between players, tools, enemies, crops, and the game world.

tulip.title: The Tulip Princess Tradition: 3 Years of Design
long: An annual tradition reignited by Jonathan Edwards (JE) College in 2022, the Tulip Princess title is bestowed upon the student who “most embodies the spirit of the tulip,” carrying themselves with dignity, strength, and camaraderie. Merchandise featuring the Tulip Princess is designed through collaboration and conversation with the elected student and the college administration, ensuring the former's wants are met while complying with the latter's needs.

I have had the honor of developing the design for the 3rd and 4th Tulip Princesses, incorporating Lee’s desired allusions to Greek muses and romantic paintings and Corson’s to justice and morality. The design for the 5th Tulip Princess is currently in progress.
short: Designed merchandise for three consecutive Tulip Princesses in collaboration with the elected students and college administration, incorporating individual themes and cultural motifs.

dndWebsite.title: DnD Dice Roller
long: As a fan of the tabletop role-playing game Dungeons & Dragons, I often find myself forgetting the set of dice needed to properly join the fun. As part of a website-design course, we were assigned to utilize HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to design a website tailored for our personal use; I elected to design an online dice roller capable of rolling a single or multiple dice at once, with their values and sums displayed to avoid repetitive calculations.

While other websites offer similar functionality, my implementation prioritizes visuals and fun interactivity as opposed to plain text, as the user can click any number of dice, each animating and changing output before landing on a single value, mimicking the tumbling of a physical die.
The website, further improved with added features and optimizations, represents a rare intersection of hobby and professional practice.
short: Created an interactive Dungeons & Dragons dice roller using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, featuring animated dice and automatic calculation of individual results and sums.
